subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: The emitted shape is literally the rule's `(operand-2 - (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n))`: Fold builds the SUM node first and Combine subtracts it from the rendered FROM operand as one nested subtrahend - not a left-to-right `((op2 - op11) - op12)`. THE PARENTHESISATION IS MEASURED, NOT ONLY READ, and the measurement is spec-derived: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL every operation rounds to 34 significant digits (8.8.1.5 / decimal128), so the two shapes disagree at the boundary. Probe k2 `SUBTRACT 0.00005 0.00005 FROM 1000000000000000000000000000000 GIVING R` (R PIC 9(31)) returned 999999999999999999999999999999 - the rule's grouping, whose intermediate 999...999.9999 is 34 digits exactly. A left-to-right fold would have rounded 999...999.99995 (35 digits) up to 1E30 at each step and stored 1000000000000000000000000000000. Ordinary cases: p2 `SUBTRACT 1 2 3 FROM 20 GIVING G1` = 14 and `SUBTRACT 1.5 2.5 FROM X GIVING G2 ROUNDED` = 6 from X=10.00; g6 several GIVING receivers each with its own ROUNDED; h1 the FROM operand as a data item (B unchanged - it is a SENDER here, not a receiver); g9/g10 a function-identifier in either sending position. The result is stored into EVERY identifier-3 (EmitGiving snapshots the value once when there is more than one receiver, 14.7.7 GR4 NOTE 3). The named golden is spec-derived (`SUBTRACT 1 FROM 5 GIVING C`, expectation 4 derived in its header) and pins the format-2 shape; it does not exercise several operand-1s, which k2/p2 do. STANDARD-BINARY IS A DECLARED NON-SUPPORT AND IS NOT MINE TO VERDICT (owner, D13): probe k3 shows `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` rejected at compile time with COBOL0806 `a processor-dependent language element (ISO Annex A.3 item 2) for which support is not claimed (4.2.6)` plus COBOL0903 (obsolete as of COBOL-2023, Annex F.2 item 3). That declination is owned by the PB260/PB261/PB281-PB283 family, so this rule's standard-binary half is out of reach by owner decision rather than by a compiler defect, and it fails LOUD - no wrong answer is reachable through it. The standard-decimal half IS reachable and IS measured below.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ArithmeticBinder.cs:76-84 BindSubtract (format 2 -> BoundSubtractGiving); src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/StatementEmitter.cs:219 Visit(BoundSubtractGiving) - `_num.Combine(_num.Render(n.From, rcv), "-", _num.Fold(n.Minuends, rcv), rcv)`; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ArithmeticEmitter.cs:49-66 EmitGiving PB228 sibling sweep (2026-10-16): the probe-only parenthesisation measurement now has a golden - 2014/pb228_subtract_standard_decimal_order's GIVING leg (SUBTRACT X Z Y FROM W GIVING G, W = 0.0008) gives 0.0008 by (operand-2 - (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n)) where native and ((W - X) - Z) - Y give 0.0004.
